chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Asadi, from Salim ibn Mukram, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The financial state of a man from the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) became difficult, so his wife said to him, 'If only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and ask him.' So he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him). When the Prophet (peace be upon him) saw him, he said: 'The one who asks us, we give to him, and the one who manages without (asking), Allah enriches him.'

The man said, 'He did not mean anyone apart from me.' So he returned to his wife and informed her. She said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) is a human being, so inform him of it.' So he went to him. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saw him, he said: 'The one who asks us, we give to him, and the one who manages without (asking), Allah enriches him,' to the extent that the man did that three times.

Then the man went away, borrowed a pickaxe, went to the mountain, climbed it, and cut firewood. Then he brought it and sold it for half a Mudd of fine flour. He returned with it and ate it. Then he went the next day and brought more than that and sold it. He did not cease working and gathering until he bought a pickaxe. Then he gathered until he bought two young camels and a slave. Then he became wealthy to the extent that he became affluent.

So he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and informed him of how he had come to ask him and how he had heard the Prophet (peace be upon him). The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I told you, the one who asks us, we give to him, and the one who manages without (asking), Allah enriches him.'

key_terms.اسْتَغْنَى: To manage without needing others; self-sufficiency

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on self-reliance versus asking for charity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the nuanced Shia understanding of *istighna* (self-sufficiency), distinguishing between the dignity of active labor and the humility of accepting charity. The companion’s repeated inquiries highlight the Prophet’s pedagogical method of guiding individuals toward economic independence through effort rather than passive reliance on alms. This narrative underscores the virtue of *istighna* as a spiritual and material state achieved through diligent work, a key theme in Twelver Shi'ite ethical teachings.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Muhammad Al Asady, from Alim Bin Mukram, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The (financial) state of a man from the companions of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> became difficult, so his wife said to him, ‘If only you would go to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and ask him<sup>saww</sup>’. So he came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So when the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> saw him, said: ‘The one who asks us<sup>saww</sup>, we<sup>saww</sup> give to him, but the one who manages without (asking), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Enrich him’.

So the man said, ‘He<sup>saww</sup> did not mean anyone apart from me’. So he returned to his wife and let her know. So she said ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> is a ‘Bashr’ (person), so let him<sup>saww</sup> know of it’. So he went over to him<sup>saww</sup>. So when Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saw him, he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who asks us<sup>saww</sup>, we<sup>saww</sup> give to him, and the one who manages without (asking), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Enrich him’, to the extent that the man did that three times.

Then the man went away, and he borrowed a pick-axe, then went to the mountain and ascended it, and cut some firewood. Then he came with it and sold it for half a Mudd (750 gms.) of flour and he returned with it. So he ate it, then went (again) the next day and came with a lot of that, and he sold it. So he did not cease working and gathering (money) until he bought a pick-axe. Then he gathered (money) until he bought two young camels and a slave. Then he was enriched to the extent that he was affluent.

So he came over to the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> and let him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> know how he had come to ask him, and how the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> made him hear (the advice). So the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> told you, the one who asks us<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, we give it to him, but the one who manages (without asking), Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Enrich him’’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Asadi from Salim ibn Mukram from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

At one time, among the companions of the Messenger of Allah, the financial conditions of one man became very difficult and his wife suggested that he see the Messenger of Allah about it. He went to the Holy Prophet and, when the Holy Prophet saw him, he said, ‘Whoever asks us for help, we help, but whoever appears to be rich when, in fact, he is not so, Allah will make him rich. ’

The man thought the Holy Prophet had addressed him only. He returned to his wife and told her the story. She said, ‘The Messenger of Allah is only a man. Let him know what you need.’ He went back and, when the Messenger of Allah saw him, he said, ‘Whoever asks us for help we help but whoever appears to be rich when, in fact, he is not so, Allah will make him rich. ’ This was repeated with that man three times.

Thereafter, he borrowed a pick and went to the mountains, climbed it and cut down a certain amount of firewood. He climbed down and sold the firewood for half a mud (a certain measure) of flour, came home and used it for food. The next day he did the same thing and saved a little on the side until he was able to buy a pick of his own and sometime later he bought two young camels and a slave and then he became rich until he became very affluent.

One day he went to see the Holy Prophet. He informed him of his whole story. The Holy Prophet said, ‘I told you, whoever asks us for help we help, but whoever appears to be rich when, in fact, he is not so, Allah will make him rich.’”
